Filmmaker Jenner Furst joins Tucker Carlson to talk about secret biotech work in China and a film that could jail Dr. Fauci. The title frames the film as a legal threat. Furst speaks as the maker of that film.

Furst lays out what his film claims about labs, virus work, and the men who funded it. He argues the paper trail leads back to Fauci and his allies. Carlson draws out the parts of the film most likely to stir a court fight. Listeners get the maker's case in full, in his own words. The library keeps the talk as a record of the claim and its aims.
uslaw-usc-t2-s288e:
Section 288e of Title 2 of the United States Code, in the chapter on the Office of Senate Legal Counsel, covers when that office steps into a case in the Senate's name. When directed under the chapter, the Counsel shall intervene, or appear as amicus curiae, in the name of the Senate or of a Senate officer, committee, subcommittee, or chairman. The case must be one where the powers and duties of Congress under the Constitution are in issue.

Intervention is allowed only if standing to intervene exists under Article III of the Constitution. The Counsel must notify the Joint Leadership Group of any case where intervention or an amicus appearance seems to be in the Senate's interest. The notice must describe the case and give the reasons behind the Counsel's view.
uslaw-usc-t2-s28e:
Section 28e of Title 2 of the United States Code covers the sharing out of surplus sets of the Precedents of Congress. Title 2 covers Congress, and this section sits in the chapter on the organization of Congress. The hosted text is the version current in twenty twenty six. The Joint Committee on Printing holds the central role.

Any set of the Precedents that was printed and bound under the linked section, and is not needed for required sharing, is covered. The Joint Committee may direct what happens to those surplus sets. Extra printing of sets under the committee's authority is also covered. The rule keeps control of a costly printed work in one joint body.
uslaw-usc-t2-s658e:
Section 658e of Title 2 of the United States Code sets mandate rules that apply in the House of Representatives. Title 2 covers Congress, and this section sits in the budget chapter, in the part on federal mandates. The hosted text is the version current in twenty twenty six. It guards a point of order against waiver by rule.

It shall not be in order in the House to consider a rule or order that waives a linked mandate section, the text states. That linked section is the core bar on unfunded mandates in bills. Disposition of points of order raised under the scheme follows in the section. The House thus binds its own future rules against quiet waiver.
